      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/30/the-academy-system-needs-a-refresh-but-now-is-the-time-for-carrick-to-trust-in-youth</link>
      <description><p>Manchester United’s most famous eras were built around their academy products, so why not give the current crop a chance to shine?</p><p>Watching Manchester United succumb <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/21/como-manchester-united-champions-league-match-report">meekly against Como</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-bournemouth-premier-league-match-report-michael-carrick">and Bournemouth</a> brought to mind questions and comparisons with yesteryear. Two of United’s most famous eras were built around their youth players: the Busby Babes and the Class of ’92. Could this be a moment for Michael Carrick to give their most talented academy products a&nbsp;meaningful&nbsp;chance?</p><p>In February 2025 I saw United beat Arsenal 3-2 in the FA Youth Cup at the Emirates Stadium. Jack and Tyler Fletcher did well for United and so did Harry Amass, a signing from Watford. Max Dowman, a generational talent, starred for Arsenal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/30/the-academy-system-needs-a-refresh-but-now-is-the-time-for-carrick-to-trust-in-youth">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/29/tottenham-season-spurs-chelsea-win-table</link>
      <description><p>Spurs had an awful start but, after an impressive win at Chelsea, they are suddenly looking up at the table</p><p>By <a href="https://theanalyst.com/">Opta Analyst</a></p><p>In reality, it was only three points. But it feels far more significant than that.</p><p>This is a fixture Tottenham almost never win. In their 34 previous visits to Chelsea in the Premier League, they had won only once. It was their first win to nil at Stamford Bridge in any competition since December 1986, nearly 40 years ago. Winning at Chelsea is huge.
